network.tdh.explainer.title: TDH
network.tdh.explainer.metadataDescriptio: What TDH is, how to read your own, and how it is calculated, specified, proved and checked every day.
network.tdh.explainer.intro: Every copy of an eligible card earns its whole days held, weighted by how rare the card is and multiplied by a boost for collecting sets.
network.tdh.explainer.why: It counts toward your Level on 6529.io. The rule is written down exactly, computed by separately written programs, and compared with 6529.io’s own calculation in public every day.
network.tdh.explainer.eligible: The Memes, Gradients and NextGen count. Meme Lab cards and received xTDH do not.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.title: TDH in a minute
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.title: Hold.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.body: Each copy you hold counts the whole days since you got it: a copy bought today adds its first day at the first daily snapshot a full day after you got it. Selling it removes its days.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.title: Weigh.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.body: Rarer cards weigh more. A card’s rate is the largest edition, FirstGM’s 3,941, divided by the card’s own edition: FirstGM itself is 1.00, and a 310-copy Meme is 12.71.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.title: Boost.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.body: Complete sets, seasons and Gradients raise one multiplier that applies to everything you hold. It starts at 1.00.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.example: Example: one copy of a 310-copy Meme, held for 100 whole days by a collector who also holds one Gradient, which adds 0.02 to the boost. Rates and boosts are those of the October 11, 2026 cycle.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.diagramDesc: Three panels. Days: 100 whole days from the purchase to the snapshot, drawn as ten groups of ten days. Rate: two bars on one scale, the largest edition, 3,941 copies, and this card, 310 copies; 3,941 divided by 310 is 12.71. Boost: a scale from 1.00 to 2.04, the highest boost on the October 11, 2026 cycle, with one Gradient at 1.02. The result is 1,296 TDH from this card.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.snapshot: TDH is computed once a day, for the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC. Ages are measured to that block’s time.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.reference: FirstGM (Meme #8) is the reference card: while its edition, which counts as 3,941, is the largest, one FirstGM copy held one whole day adds exactly one base TDH.

network.tdh.explainer.sources.label: Sources
network.tdh.explainer.sources.legend: P26 is the TDH-v1 specification, restated on the specification page; D, DEV and BUG numbers are the owner’s decisions and the specification’s deviations and issues.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.title: Checked daily, in public
network.tdh.explainer.verified.body: TDH is one written rule with several independently written programs behind it, compared with each other and with 6529.io every day.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.pro: The Python reference, a clean-room Rust reference and program B were written separately from one rule; the Rust core is the Rust reference as a library. Each is tested against the conformance vectors.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.for: A Lean 4 model, still a proposal, reproduces a real day. Its proofs show that steps inside a transaction which keep every wallet’s net movement cannot change a holding stack, while the day has a result.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.dai: From October 16, 2026, the Rust core and the Python reference run beside 6529.io every day, and the agreement is published. 6529.io switches to the Rust core about October 23.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.none: Every collector and wallet is equal, and so are the totals.

network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.title: Why can selling one card reduce TDH by more than that card’s score?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.body: The sold copy stops contributing its holding days. If the sale also breaks a set or removes a Gradient boost, your multiplier falls on the rest of your holdings too. TDH is recalculated from what you hold; it is not a permanently banked balance.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.title: Do I keep my holding time when I move a card?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.body: Moves between wallets of your confirmed consolidation keep the original acquisition time. A move outside that group starts a new holding period for the recipient. Delegation alone does not consolidate wallets. Under rule version tdh-v1.0 an identity holds at most three wallets. Four wallets that all confirm each other form one identity of three, starting from the newest link, and the fourth counts as an identity of its own (P26 §6.3). 6529.io’s consolidation guide allows a fourth wallet for links registered after its start date, so unless the rule is amended before the cutover, about October 23, 2026, such a group splits that way at the cutover: the fourth wallet’s cards no longer add to the others’ sets or boost.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.title: When does a new purchase or newly minted card count?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.body: A copy needs a completed 24-hour holding period to contribute holding days. Newly minted Memes and Gradients also need to pass the snapshot’s separate 24-hour mint-age filter. An already eligible card can complete a set before its new owner has held it for a full day.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.title: Does a full collection include the current season?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.body: Yes. You need every Meme card eligible for that snapshot, including eligible cards from the current season. When a new card becomes eligible, a previously complete collection may become incomplete. Individual season bonuses follow the eligible seasons listed above.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.title: Why isn’t tomorrow’s change exactly my daily rate?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.body: Daily rate is a guide calculated from copies held at least one whole day and the current boost. Whole-day boundaries, per-card rounding, transfers, newly eligible cards and changes in rates or boosts can all affect the next snapshot.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.title: Where does xTDH fit?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.body: xTDH is calculated separately. Receiving xTDH does not increase the base TDH explained here. Your TDH rate is an input to the xTDH system.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.title: Glossary
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.intro: The words these pages use. The first ten are all you need to read your own TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.tdh.def: Total Days Held: whole days held, weighted by rarity and multiplied by the boost, summed over everything you hold.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cycle.def: One day’s calculation. Cycle N closes at 00:00 UTC of its date; N is the number of days since January 1, 1970.
The last Ethereum block before a cycle’s 00:00 UTC. Holdings are read as of this block, and ages are measured to its time.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.edition.d: How many copies a card counts for its rate: the copies minted. A Meme with fewer than 300 minted counts at least at its claim’s mint limit, capped at 310, the size its final top-up airdrop brings it to; with no claim, the minted count. From 300 on, the minted count is the edition. Burns do not reduce it, and FirstGM’s counts 2,588 fewer.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rate.def: How much one copy-day of a card weighs: the largest Meme edition divided by the card’s edition, rounded to cents. Older pages call it the HODL rate or edition weight.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.base.def: A card’s whole days times its rate, rounded to a whole number, before the boost.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.boost.def: One multiplier for everything a collector holds, from 1.00, raised by complete sets, seasons and Gradients.
One collector as TDH counts them: a single wallet, or a group of up to three consolidated wallets. The two burn addresses also have identity records, but are never participants.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.consolida: Wallets that confirm each other on the delegation contract, so they count as one identity.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.sink.def: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0. Copies sent there are burned; the sinks keep records but are never debited, never consolidated and never count as participants.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.xtdh.def: A separate system that builds on TDH. Received xTDH does not change the TDH on these pages.
Boost schedules 1.1 to 1.4 are 6529.io’s versions of the boost, shown under Current boosts and Historic boosts. TDH-v1 is the exact written form of the current schedule, 1.4; tdh-v1.0 is its rule version.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.validator: A program, being built, that computes TDH itself every day, signs the result and agrees on it with other validators.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.term: Rust core, Rust reference, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.def: Separately written programs that compute TDH-v1: the Python reference, written with the specification; the Rust reference, written from it in a clean room; the Rust core, a copy of the Rust reference that validators will run and 6529.io runs from the cutover; and program B, a second Rust program written from the specifications alone.

network.tdh.explainer.promise: Total Days Held: the art you hold, and how long you have held it.
network.tdh.explainer.formula.label: The formula, for one card
network.tdh.explainer.formula.text: Days times rate times boost equals TDH, for each card, summed over everything you hold. For one copy of a 310-copy Meme held 100 days with one Gradient: 100 times 12.71 times 1.02 is 1,296.
network.tdh.explainer.strip.equal: Cycle of {date} (holdings at 23:59:59 UTC the day before): 6529.io’s calculation and two separately written programs agreed on all {total} TDH records, each collector’s and the two burn addresses’.

network.tdh.explainer.minute.resultNote: The Gradient earns TDH of its own on top, from its own days and rate; a collector’s TDH is the sum over every card held.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.raw.def: Whole days held times copies, before any weighting. The rate turns raw days into base TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.netting.d: Within one Ethereum transaction, each wallet’s movements of a token are added up and only the net change counts (D131). A copy that leaves and returns in one transaction never left.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.underflow: The check that no wallet ever sends a copy it does not hold. An input that fails it has no result.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.finalized: An Ethereum block that can no longer be reverted. A day has a result only once the block after its snapshot block is finalized.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.vector.de: A small test case with its exact expected values. A program conforms to TDH-v1 when it reproduces every one: 89 since October 16, 2026.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.root.def: A hash that commits to a day’s results. The cycle root binds the day, its snapshot block, the rule version with its registry hash, every wallet record outside the two sinks, each identity’s TDH per card, and the counts and total; validators will sign it. The wallet root is the tree of those wallet records, and the history root commits to every event read. Equal records give equal roots.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cutover.d: The day 6529.io switches from its current backend to the Rust core’s result, planned for about October 23, 2026 (D132).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.classes.d: How the daily comparison sorts a difference: A, a deliberate difference from the old backend; B, an old-backend bug; C, the Rust core and the Python reference disagree; D, not yet explained.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.items.def: D132 is one of the owner’s decisions; DEV-2 one of the specification’s deviations from the old backend; BUG-15 one of the old backend’s issues. Each links to its entry on the specification page.
The two separately written programs behind the planned proofs of each day’s result (D119). Program A runs the validators’ own code; program B was written from the specification alone, and its TDH code is to become the validators’ second built-in check (D125).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.memes.def: The three collections that count: The Memes, editions of many copies each; Gradients, 101 tokens of one copy each; and NextGen, whose tokens are weighed by the size of their own collection.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.firstgm.d: Meme 8, the reference card: 6,529 minted, counted as 3,941 after a recorded burn. While its edition is the largest, one FirstGM copy held one whole day adds exactly one base TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.season.de: A run of consecutive Meme ids, from a start the specification lists. Completing a season raises the boost once a later season has begun; seasons 1 to 20 carry a bonus.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.fullSet.d: At least one copy of every eligible Meme. Holding one pays every season’s bonus at once, and each further full set adds a smaller extra bonus.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.stack.def: For one card in one wallet, the list of times its copies were acquired. A send removes the copies at the end of the list, normally the newest, and each copy’s whole days come from its time.
The list of every number and address the rule uses (contracts, sinks, season starts, bonuses), fixed for each rule version and identified by its hash. Programs read it and hard-code none of it.
